title: Delhi HC: Better Possessory Title Beats Mere Occupation in a Recovery Suit
card_summary: Justice Neena Bansal Krishna dismissed a second appeal in a possession dispute over a JJ Colony property in Pappan Kalan, New Delhi. The plaintiff traced her claim through a documentary chain to the original allottee, while the defendant produced no receipt, agreement or allotment paper for a claimed oral purchase. The court held that possession is good against the whole world except a person with a better right.
card_tip: In a possession suit, a documentary chain to the original allottee beats an occupant's bare claim of an oral purchase; collect dated receipts and allotment papers, not just proof of residence.
verification_notes: Case name, citation (2026 DHC 5112), decision date (16 June 2026), the JJ Colony Pappan Kalan location, the possessory-title holding, and the rejection of the defendant's unproven oral-purchase and school-record claims are consistent across Verdictum, SCC Online Blog and LiveLaw. No stay or appeal against this ruling was found in the sources reviewed.
